failure_summary.description: Five choices added unsupported strengthening clauses, while three settled for a weaker consequence despite a stronger supported choice.

patch.reasoning: The recurring issue is choosing the wrong strength of claim: adding plausible but unproved clauses or stopping at a weaker result. A concrete, option-by-option audit makes the discriminating clauses explicit and requires selecting the strongest fully supported option.

edits.content:
## Near-duplicate option audit
When choices share a common claim but differ in qualifiers, conditions, or added conclusions, isolate the exact difference in each full option—including every conjunct, converse, scope restriction, and endpoint claim. Check each difference against the theorem or hypotheses independently: reject an option if even one clause is unsupported. Then compare the fully supported options by logical implication and choose the strongest; do not stop at a true but weaker consequence. Added properties need not be ordered by strength, so do not assume the strongest-sounding option follows from the common core.
